newsitem.title: USA: Clinton signs education bill for disabled.
newsitem.headline: Clinton signs education bill for disabled.

text.p: President Bill Clinton on Wednesday signed a reauthorization of a 22-year-old law that guarantees children with disabilities a free and appropriate education.

"Every American citizen is a person of dignity and worth, having a spirit and soul, and having the right to develop his or her full capacities," Clinton said at a White House ceremony as he signed the Individuals with Disabilities Act (IDEA) into law.

When the law was originally passed in 1975, approximately one million children with disabilities were shut out of U.S. schools and hundreds of thousands were denied services needed to enable them to learn more effectively.
The reauthorization includes several changes to the original law that raise educational standards for disabled children and helps parents track their progress.

"Education clearly will become even more important to our people in the years ahead. That is why I have made it my number one priority as president," Clinton said during an outdoor ceremony at which he was surrounded by disabled children, their advocates and lawmakers.
